page.metaTitle: Grant and Funding Opportunity Monitoring | WebMonitor.fyi
page.metaDescription: Track NIH, NSF, DOE, foundation, and state grant opportunity announcements in real time. Alerts the moment new RFPs and funding cycles open.
page.subtitle: Track grants.gov, NIH RePORTER, NSF announcements, and private foundation grant pages with alerts on every new opportunity.
page.intro: Research institutions, nonprofits, and grant-seeking organizations operate on opportunity windows that close fast. Missing an RFP by a week is often a year of waiting until the next cycle. WebMonitor.fyi tracks the public grant announcement pages — federal (grants.gov, NIH RePORTER, NSF), state, and private foundation — for new opportunities matching the keywords or topics that matter.

setup.title: Map the funders relevant to your work
setup.body: For research: NIH, NSF, DOE, NEH, NEA. For nonprofits: Ford, Rockefeller, MacArthur, sector-specific foundations. For state-level: your state's grant portal.

setup.title: Monitor the search-results URL, not the homepage
setup.body: Grants.gov and NIH RePORTER let you save a filtered search. Monitor that search URL instead of the unfiltered homepage — fewer false alerts.

setup.title: Daily intervals are right for grant monitoring
setup.body: Hourly is overkill; grants don't move that fast. Daily check at, say, 8am catches new announcements with plenty of lead time for the deadline.

setup.title: Route to the grant-development team
setup.body: Slack channel or email distribution list. The team reviews each alert and decides whether to pursue.

examples: Academic research labs tracking NIH and NSF RFP cycles
Nonprofits tracking foundation grant cycles in their issue area
State-funded programs tracking state agency grant announcements
Small businesses tracking SBA and state economic development grants
page.limits: Grant monitoring catches what the funder publishes publicly. Many private foundations operate by invitation only and never publicly post RFPs — those are outside scope. Pre-announcement intelligence (relationship-driven grant work) is a different mode.

faq.q: Can I track NIH-specific funding mechanisms?
faq.a: Yes. Use NIH RePORTER's search to narrow by activity code (R01, R21, U54) or institute (NIDDK, NCI). Monitor the filtered search URL.

faq.q: What about international funding (Horizon Europe, UKRI)?
faq.a: Yes. The European Funding and Tenders Portal and UKRI grant pages work as monitor URLs.

faq.q: Can I monitor for specific topic keywords across multiple funders?
faq.a: Yes — set one monitor per funder per topic keyword. Most grant offices run 20–40 monitors covering their funder network.
